title: fix(spec): a retired filter operator's refusal names every replacement inside the client message cap
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XQNsTJ39F7mk6zVKoTC2MU5)_

Fixes #27098

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：查询里用了已退役的过滤操作符（`$regex`、`$options`）时，`400 INVALID_FILTER` 报错现在先写"该怎么改"（`$icontains`、区分大小写用 `$contains`、真要正则就在应用代码里匹配），退役历史放到后面。只改了 spec 里那张退役表 `RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS` 两条文案的顺序和措辞。
- **为什么改**：客户端只读得到报错的前 500 个字符。原文案先讲历史、后给替代写法，`$contains` 和"在应用代码里匹配"恰好被截掉，开发者（或 AI）只知道写错了，不知道该写什么。
- **风险与回滚**：低。五处报错点都原样打印这张表，表里两条字符串调了顺序；500 字符上限、截断方式、错误信封（`code`/`status`）都没动，接受的查询集合不变。回滚即 revert。
- **先看**：`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`（`RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS` 两条 `why`）；`packages/rest/src/data-retired-filter-operator-prescription-door.test.ts`（真实 REST 门上的红绿测试）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/data-retired-filter-operator-prescription-door.test.ts`（先 build spec），预期 4/4 通过；在 `main` 上同一文件 3 条失败，报错在 `$contains` 之前就以 `…` 结束。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS` (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`) is the one table the five retired-operator refusal sites print verbatim: `driver-sql`, `driver-memory`, `driver-mongodb`, `driver-turso`'s remote transport and `objectql`'s `having`. Each site prints its own lead-in (`Filter operator "$regex" on field "title" … is RETIRED … Write "$icontains" instead.`, about 120 characters plus the field and path) and then `why`. A client reads 500 characters of it (`CLIENT_MESSAGE_MAX` in `@objectstack/types`, cut with `…`).

| | Before (`origin/main` `1900c02c`) | This head |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `$regex` `why` opens with | the retirement history (ADR-0049, how each backend read it); the alternatives come last, at about 1000 characters | the prescription: `$icontains` for a case-insensitive match, `$contains` for a case-sensitive one, a real regex means narrowing with declared operators and matching in application code; the history follows |
| `$options` `why` opens with | "was never a predicate …"; "write `$icontains`" sits mid-string | "Delete `$options`, and write `$icontains` …"; the history follows |
| What the client reads at `POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT/query` for `{ title: { $regex } }` | 500 characters ending in `…` after "an invalid", no `$contains` | 500 characters ending in `…`; the full prescription ends at character 401 (381 on `having`) |
| Cap, truncation, envelope | unchanged | unchanged |

- **One prescription source.** No refusal builder changes. The five sites keep reading `RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS[op]`; only the two strings change. `ValueDataSource` in `ui/packages/core` prints the same table and gets the same order.
- **The doc on `RetiredFilterOperatorGuidance.why`** now says prescription first, history after, and why (the 500-character client cap after each site's own lead-in).

## Tests

- `packages/rest/src/data-retired-filter-operator-prescription-door.test.ts` (new, 4 cases): the real `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` route over a real `SqlDriver` (SQLite in memory). The caller's `where` is marked `'author'` by a middleware written the way `SecurityPlugin` does it (same identity check), which is what makes `SqlDriver` show its own words rather than the withheld class sentence. Cases: `$regex` and dangling `$options` at `where`; `$regex` at `having`; control that the cap still cuts the long message at 500 with `…` and the envelope keys are `code`, `error`, `object`; control that a short refusal (354 characters) arrives whole and `$icontains` serves.
- `packages/spec/src/data/filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts` (one new case): every declared operator a `why` names in backticks first appears within its first 300 characters (500 minus the longest lead-in, with room for a long field name and path).

<details><summary>Red on the base text, green on this head</summary>

Red leg: the base blob of `filter.zod.ts` written over the fix, `@objectstack/spec` rebuilt, the tests run, then the fix restored (byte-compared to the saved copy).

```
REST door, base spec:  Tests  3 failed | 1 passed (4)
  where:  $regex reads `$contains` for a case-sensitive one: expected 'Filter operator "$regex" on field "ti…' to contain …
  having: having reads `$contains` for a case-sensitive one: expected 'Filter operator '$regex' in `having…' to contain …
  (control case was adjusted to the measured envelope keys after this run)
REST door, this head:  Tests  4 passed (4)

spec pin, base text:   Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
  $regex prescribes $icontains past the budget: expected 566 to be less than 300
spec pin, this head:   Tests  12 passed (12)
```

What the client read, base vs head (`{ title: { $regex: 'acme' } }`, SqlDriver, author-marked):

```
base: … Write "$icontains" instead. `$regex` was never declared by the Filter Protocol and is retired under ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove: … driver-memory evaluated it as a real RegExp (so it also matched "axb", and an invalid…
head: … Write "$icontains" instead. Use `$icontains` for the case-insensitive substring search `$regex` was almost always used for, or `$contains` for a case-sensitive one; a pattern that genuinely needs a regex has no filter-level replacement, so narrow with the declared operators and match in application code. Both match the comparand literally, … `$icontains` fold…
```
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The `{ $regex, $options }` pair.** Each site appends "The same field constraint also carries the retired `$options` — one `$icontains` replaces the whole shape" AFTER `why`, so it is cut for the pair, before and after this change. The lead-in and the prescription already say what to write; the sibling sentence's position lives in five builders, outside this card's surface. Noted, not changed.
- **Sibling census (report, not fixed here).** The rest suite (333 files) ran with the cut point in `@objectstack/types` instrumented (dist patched, restored byte-identical afterwards): 259 client messages reached 500 characters. Apart from synthetic fixtures (`xxxx…`) and this card's own refusal, the real 400 producers over the cap are listed in the os-dev report on the card, by producer, code and length.
- `having`'s refusal reads `retired.why` like the drivers do, so the same reorder fixes it; pinned through the same door.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: Test Files 739 passed, 1 skipped; Tests 22228 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local`: Test Files 333 passed; Tests 6556 passed, 326 skipped (the census run).
- Gates: the `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` list on this diff, each run, exit codes captured before any pipe, reconciled with `--ran` (see the os-dev report for the sheet).

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (eslint on the touched files: exit 0).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: no generated artifact reads these strings (`git grep` on the old text finds only the source).
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
